name: Wang Chongyu

tagline: Analyst by training, builder by instinct.
intro: Finance & Strategy undergraduate at Singapore Management University and Distribution Analyst intern at Conduit Group. I do the work first — fund due diligence, LP analytics, valuation — then build the systems that make it reproducible: 34 tearsheets across 8 alternative-asset sectors, a 5,146-contact LP engine, and an automated equity-research desk that briefs me every morning.
availability: Seeking internships in asset management, fund distribution, investment research, and strategy consulting.

about.heading: I can't leave a manual process alone.
body: At my internship I did the fund triage by hand once — then built the pipeline that turns a raw fund PDF into a rated, documented shelf decision. That pattern runs through everything here. I founded a licensed employment agency the same year I started university, then automated its compliance paperwork. I wanted to genuinely understand markets, so I built an equity-research desk that produces valuation work and morning briefs on a schedule. I wanted to learn faster, so I built a system that turns what I read into spaced-repetition reviews.

What drives me is straightforward: I'm obsessive about getting better — at analysis, at building, at the craft of whatever is in front of me — and I don't wait to be told to start. Every system on this page exists because I refused to do the same work twice. Put me on a team with real problems and I bring the same habit: learn it properly, do it well, then make it faster for everyone.
